name: Tarock Lungau Königrufen
description: Lungau Königrufen is a regional variant of Austrian Königrufen played in the Lungau region of Salzburg. It is known for being a faster, sharper game with fewer, more decisive contracts and a streamlined counting process.

overview.description: Lungau Königrufen is a regional variant of Austrian Königrufen played in the Lungau region of Salzburg. It is known for being a faster, sharper game with fewer, more decisive contracts and a streamlined counting process.

history.origins: Lungau Königrufen is a streamlined regional variant of Austrian Königrufen played in the Salzburger Lungau in central Austria. It developed from the traditional Tarock game with a reduced set of contracts (Sechserdreier, Rufer mit Spatz, Rufer mit Uhu, Dreier) and simplified card counting, producing a sharper, faster game than forms played elsewhere in Austria. Regular tournaments are held in the region; the variant is maintained and documented as a distinct local tradition.
timeline: 20th century: played in Salzburger Lungau; regional tournaments documented.
history.cultural: Strong local following in Salzburg province.

rules.objective: Win tricks containing valuable cards; take a majority of card points (36 or more out of 71); score game points from the contract and bonuses; losers pay winners per game point.
rules.gameplay: Bidding. Contracts include Rufer, Solo, Sechserdreier. Calling a King. Talon usage depends on bid. Play follows standard Tarock rules (follow suit/trump).

scoring.description: Card points (71 total); 36+ wins the game. Contract and bonuses in game points; losers pay winners per game point (e.g. 10 cents per point).
scoring.winCondition: The team with a majority of card points (36 or more out of 71) wins the game. Bonuses (Trull, Four Kings, Pagat Ultimo, Uhu, King Ultimo, etc.) add or subtract game points. Net score determines payment from losers to winners.
